claim: the regularisation parameter is an unreported degree of freedom in Casson haemodynamics
method: gap-map step 6 (claim test) over a deduplicated Crossref+PubMed corpus; TITLE+ABSTRACT metadata only

depletion.pair: CONTROL haemodynamic x wall shear stress
depletion.note: control is ENRICHED, so the method detects co-occurrence where it exists

depletion.pair: CONTROL Casson x wall shear stress
depletion.note: WEAK control - itself depleted, so it supports the instrument less than the haemodynamic pair does

examples: A hyperbolic-regularized Casson model for pulsatile blood flow simulation in a rigid artery

limits: Title+abstract only. A regularisation cap is a METHODS detail that rarely reaches an abstract, so 1.4% is NOT a reporting rate - it is a visibility rate, and the reporting question needs FULL TEXT.
Absolute counts are lower bounds; the relative comparison against the enriched control is what carries information.
Query-set dependent. Three query families per pillar is a smell test, not a systematic review.
A direct precedent was surfaced and must be read before any novelty claim: the hyperbolic-regularized Casson paper sits squarely in the intersection.
outcome: The two literatures are structurally disconnected (ratio 0.10, p=6e-18, against an enriched control at 1.96). That supports a DISCONNECTION claim. It does NOT establish a reporting rate, and the mechanism itself is not novel - see Frigaard & Nouar (2005).
